# Md Tanvir Arafin — Academic Website

> Dr. Md Tanvir Arafin is a leading researcher in hardware security and secure computer architecture, and a tenure-track Assistant Professor in the Department of Cyber Security Engineering at George Mason University (GMU), Fairfax, VA. He is a principal investigator on multiple NSF-funded projects spanning secure accelerators for AI/ML models, transportation cybersecurity, and IoT/edge security. Research areas include side-channel attacks, fault injection, post-quantum cryptography acceleration, autonomous systems security, and hardware-derived roots of trust (PUFs, TRNGs, HSMs).

## Research Focus

- Hardware security: side-channel attacks, fault injection, physical unclonable functions (PUFs), secure accelerators
- Autonomous systems security: LiDAR spoofing, ROS2 vulnerabilities, vehicular network attacks (CAN bus)
- Post-quantum cryptography acceleration: NTT, hash-based schemes on spatial/reconfigurable architectures
- AI/ML security: adversarial examples, model inversion, membership inference, backdoor attacks
- Verifiable computing: zkSNARKs, sum-check protocol, GPU acceleration
- Transportation cybersecurity: automotive security, connected and autonomous vehicles
